rules.rationale: This is the terminating base equation of the mergeThirdFrom mathematical summary: once I is at or beyond N, the remaining output suffix is empty. It defines a proof term and does not execute or observe the Python model.

This is the divisible-by-three recurrence for mergeThirdFrom, defining the next summary element from the sorted third-position sequence and recurring at I + 1. It is a mathematical summary equation rather than an operational MPY rule.

This is the complementary recurrence for mergeThirdFrom, defining a non-third position from the original sequence and recurring at I + 1. Together with the other guarded cases it defines the summary and does not replace source execution.

This simplification rule introduces sortThirdResult as a folding name for the exact complete mergeThirdFrom term. Its orientation is solver-facing, but its role is definitional abbreviation of a named proof summary.

This simplifier asserts the zero-length consequence for the already defined sortThirdResult summary. Stage 1 uses the rule in the compiled verification theory and provides no earlier kprove of this exact guarded statement against a module omitting it, so it is an additional trusted mathematical fact rather than a proved derived lemma.

This is list-concatenation associativity, a reusable mathematical fact about the pre-existing valSeqConcat function. Although Stage 1 describes a structural-induction justification, prove.sh compiles this simplification rule before all proofs and contains no separate proof of the exact equation without the rule.

This is the right-identity law for the pre-existing valSeqConcat function. Its comment calls it derived by structural induction, but Stage 1 does not first prove the exact statement in a module that omits the simplifier, so the finalized K proof trusts it as a domain lemma.
